hypotheses.claim: An approved cross-zone escalation reaches the receiving SE only as a generic 'Day Plan updated' in-app notice with no cross-zone framing, and no human in the TARGET zone (its ZM) is told at all — so the receiving side learns of the hand-off by noticing a new stop, which is a MANUAL hand-off under the standing spine rule.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: SpineDayPlanNotifier is a real NotificationService writer, so the SE genuinely is pushed and the hand-off is automatic; the target ZM simply is not a required recipient.
hypotheses.altCheck: grep -rn 'DAY_PLAN_NOTIFIER' apps/backend/src --include=*.module.ts — SpineDayPlanNotifier is bound, not the Logging stub; but grep for notify targeting targetZoneId in cross-zone-escalation.service.ts returns nothing (only notifyHomeZm :312 and notifyRole :333, neither of which resolves the target zone).

hypotheses.claim: The approve two-phase orphan is reachable in practice, not just theoretically: an escalation stranded PENDING on an already-assigned ticket stays in the CSM queue permanently and every retry returns 409 TICKET_ALREADY_ASSIGNED, with no admin path to clear it.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: deny/defer still work on the stranded row, so the CSM can clear the queue by denying it — cosmetic, not a P3.
hypotheses.altCheck: decide() at :262-264 only checks isOpen(status), so DENY on a stranded PENDING row does succeed — but it writes DENIED onto an escalation whose ticket is assigned, and notifyHomeZm :278 then tells the home ZM the request was refused. The escape hatch produces a false record, which is why this needs a persist walk rather than a code read.

hypotheses.claim: The `crossZoneEscalations: { none: {} }` sweep predicate (:83) means a Platinum ticket whose escalation was ever DENIED, DEFERRED-and-lapsed or orphaned can never auto-escalate again, so the Platinum SLA guarantee silently expires after one escalation per ticket for the ticket's whole life.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: One escalation per ticket is the intended rule — the docstring at :73 says 'one escalation per Ticket' — and a denied Platinum is meant to travel the reEscalateToOps rung instead of re-sweeping.
hypotheses.altCheck: The docstring :73 does say one per ticket, and reEscalateToOps :201 does exist for DENIED AUTO rows — but CZ-05 shows that rung is unreachable from the UI, and flag() :127-130 deliberately uses the narrower status-scoped predicate for the same question, so the two paths disagree. Which is intended cannot be read off the code.

hypotheses.claim: Because cross-zone.controller.ts:113 discards actedAsRole, a CSM acting in an absent ZM's zone can also press the ZM-only re-escalate endpoint (or is wrongly blocked from it), since zmOwnsZone :287 was written to read the acting role that never arrives.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: @Roles('ZONAL_MANAGER') at controller :103 blocks a CSM at the guard before zmOwnsZone is ever consulted, so the dead branch changes no actual permission outcome — it is documentation rot, not a permissions hole.
hypotheses.altCheck: controller :103 is @Roles('ZONAL_MANAGER') and the guard is class-level (:37), which supports the alternative for re-escalate specifically; but zmOwnsZone is also the gate for flag() (:124), whose @Roles at :56 DOES include CENTRAL_SERVICE_MANAGER — so a CSM reaches zmOwnsZone with actedAsRole null and takes the :288 branch that returns true for any zone. Whether that is intended CSM breadth or an unintended bypass needs a role walk.

hypotheses.claim: targetZoneId is never validated against the chosen SE's actual zone, so an approved escalation can record a target zone the SE does not belong to — making every per-zone cross-zone metric and the C8 report unreliable at the source.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: The UI will eventually derive seId from a zone-filtered picker, so the pair is consistent by construction and no backend check is needed.
hypotheses.altCheck: CrossZonePage.tsx:56-60 takes both values from free-text window.prompt with no picker at all, and override.assignTicket :666 checks only the TICKET's home zone via inScope, :668 looks the engineer up by id alone — no zone comparison on either side. The construction the alternative relies on does not exist today; whether a mismatched pair actually persists needs a save-and-reload.
